translation: 不复存在，灭绝，消亡；消失；失踪
original_sentence: Over the past 50 years, about 17 per cent of the rainforest has disappeared due to human activities such as agriculture and cattle farming.
readingExamples: Over the past 50 years, about 17 per cent of the rainforest has disappeared due to human activities such as agriculture and cattle farming.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to cease to be visible; to pass out of sight suddenly or gradually
(2) vi. to stop existing; to be lost, wiped out or made extinct
(3) vi. (of a person) to go away unexpectedly and cannot be found; to vanish
(4) vi. to be no longer available or used; to fade away

posExamples.sentence: One moment the little boat was riding the crest of a wave; the next it had disappeared into the trough, and my heart froze in my chest. （读后续写·海上惊险）
I am deeply worried that, unless we act now, these traditional crafts will quietly disappear, taking with them centuries of irreplaceable wisdom. （应用文·呼吁保护）
When a species disappears, it does not vanish alone; it drags with it a whole web of life that had depended on its existence for millions of years. （议论文·生物多样性）
As the years passed, her fear of the dark gradually disappeared, replaced by a quiet curiosity about the shapes that moved beyond the window. （读后续写·成长心理）

wordForms.other: 反义：appear (出现) / appearance (n. 出现)

idioms.example: By the time the guards reached the tower, the prisoner had vanished as if he had disappeared into thin air, leaving only an open window and a rope of knotted sheets. （读后续写·悬疑逃脱）

idioms.idiom: disappear off the face of the earth
idioms.example: After the scandal, he seemed to disappear off the face of the earth, and not one of his old friends ever heard from him again. （读后续写·人物失踪）

collocations.example: She waved until the train had disappeared from view, then turned away, blinking back the tears she had promised not to shed. （读后续写·离别）
The stranger pressed the note into my hand and disappeared into the crowd before I could utter a word of thanks. （读后续写·神秘人物）

collocations.phrase: disappear into the crowd / darkness / distance
collocations.translation: 消失在人群/黑暗/远方中
collocations.example: With a final wave, the old sailor disappeared into the grey distance, and the harbour felt suddenly, achingly empty. （读后续写·告别·怅然）
The wallet she had left on the bench had disappeared without a trace, and with it her last few coins for the bus home. （读后续写·丢失）
As the fever broke, the pain in his joints gradually disappeared, and for the first time in weeks he slept the whole night through. （读后续写·康复）

collocations.phrase: disappear due to / because of sth
collocations.example: Countless small streams have disappeared due to over-farming and careless waste, and with them a way of life that once defined the region. （议论文·环境）
The magician's smooth flick of the wrist made the coin disappear, and the children gasped in pure delight. （读后续写·魔术表演）
Whole civilisations have disappeared from history, their proud cities now buried beneath silent desert sand. （议论文·文明兴衰）

synonyms.translation: 突然消失,消失得无影无踪
synonyms.example: The morning mist vanished the instant the sun climbed above the hills, revealing a valley washed clean and glittering. （读后续写·环境）
synonyms.usage: 比'disappear'更突然、更彻底、更有文学色彩,续写中制造神秘或惊叹感首选;'disappear'语气中性,泛用

synonyms.example: The old photograph had faded almost to nothing, yet in her memory that summer afternoon remained as vivid as ever. （读后续写·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 强调'渐渐、由浓变淡'的消失过程,多用于颜色、声音、记忆、希望;'disappear'既可突然也可渐渐

synonyms.example: Unless urgent measures are taken, this rare orchid will die out within our own lifetime. （议论文·物种保护）
synonyms.usage: 专指物种、习俗、语言等因失去生存条件而彻底'灭绝';'disappear'含义更广,可指一切事物消失

advancedExpressions.expression: one moment ..., the next sb./sth. had disappeared
advancedExpressions.example: One moment he was laughing beside the campfire; the next he had disappeared into the pitch-black forest, and only his footprints told us he had ever been there. （one moment...the next时间对比,制造突变悬念）

advancedExpressions.expression: if we fail to act, ... will disappear forever
advancedExpressions.example: If we fail to act today, these age-old folk songs will disappear forever, and future generations will never know the melodies that once carried our ancestors' joys and sorrows. （if条件句+forever强调不可逆,增强紧迫感）

advancedExpressions.expression: when ... disappears, ... disappears with it
advancedExpressions.example: When a language disappears, an entire way of seeing the world disappears with it, and humanity grows quietly poorer. （when从句+disappears with it顶针,凸显连锁损失）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The dog ran away and we couldn't find it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In the blink of an eye the frightened puppy had disappeared into the tangled undergrowth, and though we called until our voices cracked, only the wind answered from the darkening woods. （读后续写·寻找+环境）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In the blink of an eye状语提速 + disappear into具体化去向 + though让步从句渲染徒劳 + only the wind answered拟人收束气氛

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: That主语从句提前 + 三副词递进(silently, irreversibly, unnoticed) + not merely...but对比升级 + at our peril正式收尾强化警示

original_sentence: Over the past 50 years, about 17 per cent of the rainforest has disappeared due to human activities such as agriculture and cattle farming.
readingExamples: Over the past 50 years, about 17 per cent of the rainforest has disappeared due to human activities such as agriculture and cattle farming.
definitionEn:
(1) prep. because of; as a result of; caused by
(2) prep. (used after a linking verb) attributable to; owing to a particular cause or reason

uncommonMeanings.meaning: be due to do sth 预计/预定做某事
uncommonMeanings.example: Rose is due to start school in January, and the whole family has been quietly counting down the days ever since. （应用文/记叙·安排）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: be due 预定到达；预产（The train is due in five minutes.）
uncommonMeanings.example: The train is due in five minutes, so she stood at the very edge of the platform, her whole body leaning toward the coming reunion. （读后续写·等待·重逢）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 到期，应交（My essay is due next Friday.）
uncommonMeanings.example: My essay is due next Friday, yet the blank page still stared back at me, as blank and merciless as ever. （读后续写·拖延·压力）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: be due for sth 该……了，到了该得到某物的时候（due for promotion）
uncommonMeanings.example: Everyone in the office agreed that, after so many quiet years of hard work, she was more than due for promotion. （议论文/记叙·职场·公平）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 应有的，适当的（after due consideration 经过适当考虑）
uncommonMeanings.example: After due consideration, and with a heavy but honest heart, the committee decided to award the prize to the quietest boy in the class. （读后续写·评选·公正）

posExamples.sentence: The match was called off due to the sudden storm, and a crowd of disappointed children pressed their faces against the rain-streaked windows. （读后续写·扫兴场景）
I regret to inform you that the outing has been postponed due to the unexpected weather warning issued this morning. （应用文·通知）
Much of the recent decline in wildlife is due not to natural causes but to human greed, and this is a truth we can no longer afford to deny. （议论文·环境责任）
Her sudden confidence on stage was due entirely to the quiet encouragement of a teacher who had believed in her from the very first day. （读后续写·师恩）

idioms.example: Be patient, the old carpenter said with a knowing smile; the wood will teach you its secrets in due course. （读后续写·师徒·耐心）

idioms.translation: 恕我直言,冒昧地说(委婉表达不同意见)
idioms.example: With all due respect, sir, I believe the plan overlooks the very people it claims to help. （应用文·辩论/建议）

idioms.translation: 公平地对待某人,承认某人的长处
idioms.example: To give him his due, even his rivals admitted that no one had worked harder to save the flooded village. （读后续写·公正评价）

collocations.phrase: due to sth = because of （由于，因为）
collocations.example: Over the past 50 years, about 17 per cent of the rainforest has disappeared due to human activities such as agriculture and cattle farming. （说明文·课文原句·环境）

collocations.phrase: be largely / mainly / partly due to
collocations.translation: 很大程度上/主要/部分由于
collocations.example: Her success in the finals was largely due to the countless dawns she had spent training while the rest of the town still slept. （读后续写·励志）
Scientists agree that the sharp rise in global temperatures is due largely to human activities such as burning fossil fuels. （议论文·气候）
The remarkable recovery of the lake was due to years of patient effort by ordinary villagers. （议论文·环保成效）
The guest speaker is due to arrive at three, so please make sure the hall is ready by half past two. （应用文·活动安排）

collocations.translation: 由于……这一事实(后接从句)
collocations.example: The event was rescheduled due to the fact that half the volunteers had fallen ill during the flu season. （应用文·通知/报告）
Passengers are kindly asked to expect delays due to the ongoing repair work on the main line. （应用文·公告）

synonyms.example: Owing to the heavy fog, the ferry service was suspended, stranding dozens of weary travellers on the quay. （读后续写·滞留）
synonyms.usage: 与'due to'意思几乎相同,但语法上更'纯正'——传统语法认为'owing to'可直接放句首作状语,'due to'严格上多接在be动词后;考试中两者常可互换,应用文/议论文更显正式

synonyms.translation: 多亏,由于(多含积极色彩)
synonyms.example: Thanks to the tireless efforts of the rescue team, not a single life was lost in the disaster. （读后续写·感恩）
synonyms.usage: 同表原因,但通常带感激或正面结果的语气;若结果是坏事则常用反讽;'due to'语气中性,好坏皆可

synonyms.example: On account of his failing eyesight, the old scholar had learned to read the world through his fingertips and his memory. （读后续写·人物·坚韧）
synonyms.usage: 较正式、书面的因果短语，后接名词/动名词，常见于议论文与正式说明；'due to'同样偏书面但更通用

synonyms.synonym: be caused by / be the result of
synonyms.example: The widening desert, scientists insist, is the result of decades of reckless farming rather than any change in the sky. （议论文·归因）
synonyms.usage: 作谓语结构表因果，可与 be due to 互换以避免重复；the result of 强调'……造成的结果'这一名词化表达，句式更凝练

synonyms.example: Because of one act of kindness from a stranger, her whole outlook on the world began to change. （读后续写·转折）
synonyms.usage: 最口语化、最通用的因果介词短语,后接名词/动名词,任何文体皆宜;'due to'略正式,书面感更强

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., due in no small part to ...
advancedExpressions.example: She stood taller now, due in no small part to the letter still folded warm against her heart. （due in no small part to强调'很大程度上',含蓄点出原因）

advancedExpressions.expression: We regret that ... due to circumstances beyond our control
advancedExpressions.example: We regret that the charity concert must be postponed due to circumstances entirely beyond our control. （固定得体表达,委婉说明客观原因）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., due not to ... but to ...

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Row upon row铺陈画面 + due to替换because of提升书面感 + 具体化(three merciless months) + 拟人(merciless)渲染无情

posExamples.sentence: As dawn broke over the terraced fields, the old farmer knelt in the mud, and I suddenly understood that agriculture, to him, was not merely a livelihood but a lifelong conversation with the land. （读后续写·乡村劳作·画面感）

definitionEn:

synonyms.example: The gentle giant would not harm a fly, for all its fearsome size. （读后续写·反差）

synonyms.example: One thoughtless comment threatened to ruin the friendship they had spent years building. （读后续写·人际）

advancedExpressions.expression: the damage, though visible everywhere, could not ...

advancedExpressions.expression: before the damage becomes irreversible, let us ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The flood damaged many houses.

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not damage the environment for money.

original_sentence: For another thing, due to the Amazon’s hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build up enough nutrients.
readingExamples: For another thing, due to the Amazon’s hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build up enough nutrients.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the general weather conditions typical of a particular region over a long period
(2) n. the general attitude, mood, or set of conditions prevailing in a place, organisation, or period (e.g. political climate)
(3) n. an area or region considered with reference to its typical weather

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （社会、政治、经济等的）氛围，风气，形势
uncommonMeanings.example: In the tense political climate of those years, a single careless remark could cost a person everything, so most people learned to weigh each word before speaking. （读后续写/议论文·时代氛围）

posExamples.sentence: Stepping off the plane into the sticky tropical climate, she felt the heat wrap around her like a damp blanket, and knew at once that this journey would change her forever. （读后续写·异国·感官描写）
I am writing to invite you to our school forum on climate change, where students will share simple yet powerful ways to protect the only planet we call home. （应用文·邀请信）
Tackling climate change is not the duty of governments alone; it demands the small, daily choices of every ordinary citizen who dares to care. （议论文·环保责任）
Due to the Amazon's hot and humid climate, the soil struggles to build up nutrients, making the rainforest far more fragile than its lush appearance suggests. （议论文·自然科普）

collocations.example: Rising sea levels are among the most alarming signs that climate change is no longer a distant threat but a present reality. （议论文·环境）

collocations.translation: 全球变暖 / 变暖的气候
collocations.example: A warming climate is quietly redrawing the map of where crops can grow and where deserts will spread. （议论文·农业）

collocations.translation: 热带 / 温带 / 干旱气候
collocations.example: The date palm thrives in a dry climate that would kill most other fruit trees. （说明文·植物）
Despite the harsh climate of the plateau, the herders had learned to live in quiet harmony with the land. （读后续写·适应）
It took the settlers years to adapt to the freezing climate of their new mountain home. （读后续写·移居）
Young people around the world are demanding that leaders treat the climate crisis with the urgency it truly deserves. （议论文·呼吁）
In the current economic climate, many graduates are choosing security over ambition when they hunt for jobs. （议论文·社会）
A good leader nurtures a climate of trust in which every member feels free to speak the truth. （议论文·领导力）

synonyms.example: The weather turned suddenly, and dark clouds swallowed the sun that had shone all morning. （读后续写·转折）
synonyms.usage: 指某时某地短期的天气状况（今天、此刻）；climate 指某地区长期、总体的气候规律

synonyms.example: A warm, welcoming atmosphere filled the little café the moment the fire was lit. （读后续写·场景）
synonyms.usage: 对应 climate 的'氛围'义，指某场合当下的感觉/情调；climate（氛围义）更偏长期、大范围的社会风气

synonyms.example: The rescue was called off because the conditions on the mountain had become too dangerous. （记叙·处境）
synonyms.usage: 泛指各种客观情况（天气、经济、工作等），需搭配语境；climate 特指气候或长期整体氛围

advancedExpressions.expression: the harsh climate ..., yet ...
advancedExpressions.example: The harsh climate of the far north would break most spirits within a season, yet in this frozen wilderness the boy discovered a strength he had never known he had. （yet 转折+环境衬托人物，续写设景）

advancedExpressions.expression: in the face of a changing climate, it falls to each of us to ...
advancedExpressions.example: In the face of a rapidly changing climate, it falls to each of us to rethink how we travel, what we buy, and how much we waste. （in the face of 面对+it falls to sb. to 责任落实，倡议信主体）

advancedExpressions.expression: climate change is not a matter of ... but of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Climate change is not a matter of if, but of when and how severely; to delay action any longer is to gamble recklessly with our children's future. （not...but 强调+gamble with 比喻警示，凸显紧迫）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The climate there was very hot and she felt uncomfortable.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The sweltering climate pressed down on her like an invisible weight, drawing beads of sweat from her brow and sapping the strength from her legs with every dragging step. （读后续写·感官描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: sweltering 精准形容词 + press down like 明喻 + 现在分词并列(drawing...sapping) + 细节动作(beads of sweat / dragging step)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Everyone should do something about climate change.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that each of us shouldered our share of responsibility in the fight against climate change, for the planet cannot wait for someone else to act first. （议论文·呼吁句）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that + 虚拟语气(shouldered) 表紧迫 + shoulder one's share of responsibility 正式搭配 + for 引出理由从句

另一方面，由于亚马逊炎热的气候，土壤很难积聚足够的养分。

translation: (a)增强(体质/力量)；(b)建立，开发；(c)积累，积聚；(d)逐渐增强，变得严重
original_sentence: For another thing, due to the Amazon’s hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build up enough nutrients.
readingExamples: For another thing, due to the Amazon’s hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build up enough nutrients.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to increase or develop gradually over a period of time, or to make something do this
(2) v. to gradually create or accumulate something (a reputation, strength, a collection) through effort
(3) v. to give someone more confidence or make something seem more important, often through praise or publicity
(4) v. to cover an area of land with buildings

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 增强（体质/力量），使强壮（give him soup to build him up；build up one's strength）
uncommonMeanings.example: His grandmother made a rich broth every evening to build him up, until the pale, trembling boy of spring had grown sturdy and brown by autumn. （读后续写·康复·亲情）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 建立，开发（built up a successful business）
uncommonMeanings.example: From a single rented stall, she had built up a successful business that now fed a hundred families besides her own. （议论文/读后续写·奋斗·白手起家）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 积累，积聚（built up a fine art collection；the soil to build up enough nutrients）
uncommonMeanings.example: For another thing, due to the Amazon's hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build up enough nutrients. （说明文·课文原句·自然科普）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 逐渐增强，变得严重（frustration and anger can build up）
uncommonMeanings.example: Swallowed silently day after day, frustration and anger can build up until, at the smallest spark, they burst out in ways we later cannot forgive. （议论文·情绪管理）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 过分吹捧；为……大肆造势（常带贬义）
uncommonMeanings.example: The whole village had built the newcomer up as some kind of hero, so when he turned out to be an ordinary, awkward man, the disappointment was almost cruel. （读后续写·期望落空·反差）

posExamples.sentence: As the fever refused to break, a knot of dread began to build up in her chest, tightening with every shallow breath her little brother took beneath the thin blanket. （读后续写·危机·心理描写）
I am writing to suggest that we build up a small library of donated books in the classroom, so that every student, regardless of family background, can enjoy the quiet pleasure of reading. （应用文·建议信）
Genuine confidence is not handed to us overnight; rather, it is built up slowly, through countless small victories over the fears that once seemed insurmountable. （议论文·成长与自信）
Over the years, the old craftsman had built up a reputation for honesty that no amount of advertising could ever have bought. （读后续写·人物·口碑）

wordForms.adjective: built-up (adj. 建筑密集的;逐渐形成的)

collocations.phrase: build up one's strength / build sb up
collocations.translation: 增强体质/力量；把某人养壮
collocations.example: The coach urged us to build up our strength gradually, warning that shortcuts would only end in injury. （读后续写·体育训练）

collocations.translation: 建立/开发（一份成功的）事业
collocations.example: Over twenty patient years he built up a successful business, brick by brick, from a workshop no bigger than a garden shed. （读后续写·奋斗·励志）

collocations.phrase: build up enough nutrients (in the soil)
collocations.example: In cooler forests the soil has time to build up enough nutrients, but under the Amazon's fierce heat everything decays and washes away too fast. （说明文·科普·课文延伸）

collocations.phrase: build up a collection / a fine art collection
collocations.translation: 积攒一批藏品／一批精美艺术藏品
collocations.example: Over a lifetime the quiet schoolteacher had built up a fine art collection that, to everyone's astonishment, he left entirely to the town museum. （读后续写·人物·奉献）

collocations.translation: （挫败/愤怒/压力）逐渐积聚、变得严重
collocations.example: As the deadline approached, the tension in the office continued to build up until no one dared to speak above a whisper. （读后续写·氛围渲染）
A single word of encouragement from her mentor did more to build up her confidence than a year of private tutoring. （读后续写·师生鼓励）
It takes decades to build up a good reputation, yet a single careless act can tear it down in a moment. （议论文·诚信主题）
Regular exercise helps the body build up immunity against common illnesses. （应用文·健康倡议）
By setting aside a little each month, the young couple slowly built up enough savings to open their own bookshop. （读后续写·奋斗·励志）
The music built up to a thunderous climax, and the entire hall rose to its feet as one. （读后续写·演出·高潮）

synonyms.example: Snow accumulated on the windowsill hour after hour, until the whole street lay hushed beneath a blanket of white. （读后续写·环境描写）
synonyms.usage: 更正式、更书面,强调数量一点点增多的结果;build up 更口语,可指抽象的信心、名声,也可指物质的堆积

synonyms.example: Through years of patient practice, she developed a steady hand and a keen eye that few surgeons could match. （议论文·能力养成）
synonyms.usage: 强调从无到有、由弱变强的整体成长过程;build up 更突出"逐步增加"这一渐进动作本身

synonyms.example: Frequent letters strengthened the bond between the two old friends despite the ocean that lay between them. （应用文·友谊）
synonyms.usage: 强调使已有的东西变得更牢固;build up 可从零开始逐步搭建,strengthen 通常针对既有基础

advancedExpressions.type: 词汇拓展·动词 + up 短语家族（辨析）
advancedExpressions.expression: build on / make up / take up / set up / bring up / put up
advancedExpressions.example: 同类 up 短语一起记：build on（在……基础上进一步发展）；make up（弥补/构成/编造/化妆）；take up（占据/开始从事）；set up（建立，创办）；bring up（抚养；提出）；put up（举起/张贴/留宿）。与 build up（增强/建立/积累/加剧）成组对比，写作时按语义精准选用。

advancedExpressions.expression: little by little, a ... began to build up within sb.
advancedExpressions.example: Little by little, a quiet determination began to build up within him, until at last he squared his shoulders and stepped into the storm. （渐进副词+抽象名词具象化,续写蓄势段）

advancedExpressions.expression: by doing ..., we can gradually build up ...
advancedExpressions.example: By recycling just one bottle a day, we can gradually build up a cleaner, greener campus for every generation to come. （从小事切入的号召句式，倡议书结尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: what takes years to build up can be destroyed in ...
advancedExpressions.example: What takes years of honest effort to build up can be destroyed in a single reckless moment — this is why integrity must never be treated as negotiable. （对比+因果，诚信类论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She slowly got her confidence back.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Bit by bit, like a tide creeping back over sun-baked sand, her confidence built up again, until the girl who had once trembled before the class now met every gaze without flinching. （读后续写·心理转变+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: bit by bit渐进节奏 + like a tide...明喻 + until引导结果状语呈现前后反差 + who once...定语从句强化对比

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should protect our school's good name.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is incumbent upon each of us to safeguard the fine reputation our school has built up over the decades, for such trust, once broken, can rarely be mended. （议论文·正式论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is incumbent upon sb. to do正式责任句式 + built up over the decades现在完成时强调积累 + for引导原因 + once broken过去分词短语作条件

classPractice.question: Due to the Amazon's hot climate, it is difficult for the soil to build ____ enough nutrients.
classPractice.note: 课文原句：build up 积累，积聚（养分）；it is difficult for sb/sth to do 中it作形式主语。

original_sentence: Global warming, for example, is a major problem caused by greenhouse gases.
readingExamples: Global warming, for example, is a major problem caused by greenhouse gases.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. affecting or including the whole world
(2) adj. considering or including all parts of something; general or overall
(3) adj. (computing) applying to or affecting the whole of a file, program or system rather than one part of it

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 全局的,整体考虑的;总体的
uncommonMeanings.example: Instead of fussing over a single misplaced comma, the editor urged her to take a more global view of the essay and ask whether the argument as a whole held together. （读后续写/议论文·整体思维）

posExamples.sentence: Standing at the summit at dawn, she watched the sunlight spill across ridge after ridge and suddenly grasped how small her worries were against the vast, breathing body of the global wilderness. （读后续写·壮景·感悟）
I am writing to invite you to our school's Global Culture Festival, where students from over twenty countries will share the food, music and stories of their homelands. （应用文·邀请函）

collocations.example: Global warming has caused glaciers that stood for thousands of years to melt away within a single lifetime. （议论文·环境）

advancedExpressions.expression: as global citizens, we bear the responsibility to ...

advancedExpressions.expression: only through global cooperation can ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many countries are working together to fight global warming.
